steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook linguine at a boil until tender yet firm to the bite, about 11 minutes.

Meanwhile, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic, and sauté briefly to release flavor. Add cream; heat just to boiling, stirring frequently. Reduce heat to low; stir in shrimp, parsley, basil, and thyme. Continue cooking until shrimp are just heated through; remove sauce from heat.
Drain pasta and toss lightly with cream sauce. Add Parmesan cheese, salt, and pepper to taste; toss again and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Shrimp Linguine
raw_recipe.description: This shrimp linguine recipe with parsley, basil, and thyme in a dreamy garlic and cream sauce is great for a family dinner and good enough for guests!

review.reviewBody: Delicious. I used all fresh herbs (including 1/2 c. chopped fresh parsley) and I think it makes a big difference in taste. Anytime a recipe calls for shrimp, I cook the shrimp in boiling water for 3 minutes, then rinse with cold water to stop the cooking process. At the last minute, I add the shrimp to the sauce and heat just long enough to warm the shrimp. In my opinion, slow cooked shrimp turns out "spongy" and "mushy". Some reviewers said this recipe was a little bland, so I added 4-5 tablespoons of cayenne pepper to the boiling water before cooking the shrimp. YUM! Thanks, will definitely make this again.

I tweaked this recipe a bit to make it less fattening but it was absolutely delicious. Used half shrimp, half scallops. Coated pan with a small amount of extra virgin olive oil, sauteed the shrimp and garlic till barely cooked then removed from pan. Added sliced mushrooms and browned them. Then I added 1/2 container of light herb and garlic cream cheese and 3/4 cup of the pasta water plus fresh basil, thyme, Italian parsley. Simmered until thickened then added the shrimp and garlic. Served over pasta - with freshly grated parmigiano - fabulous!

This was easy and delicious!!!! Do not substitute the heavy whipping cream, it makes the dish. In fact, you can add just a little more! I did strain the garlic out of the cream so not to bite into pieces of garlic. For the shrimp, I purchased the Tequila Lime Shrimp from Costco; already seasoned and tasted great! It’s a favorite and will be used often.

I did make some changes but think it would be excellent, if extremely rich and perhaps a tiny bit bland, as written. My main complaint is that it does not make enough sauce for that amount of pasta — the amount of shrimp is fine but it needs more liquid. My changes: 2% milk plus cornstarch, 1/3 the butter (plus a generous spoonful of light sour cream at the end). I doubled the garlic, used dried basil and subbed a small amount of green onion for the parsley (my parsley was a little sad looking), plus I added a few generous pinches of Cajun seasoning. People put their own Parmesan on. Oh yes, and I added some sliced sautéed mushrooms; I bet asparagus would also be great.

This was very tasty and easy as well. I wanted to incorporate veggies into the meal so I cut up onions and red peppers and mushrooms to cook with the garlic. Other than that I followed the recipe. Served it over linguine with parmesan cheese.

We made this last night and it was one of the best pasta dishes to date. We used fresh herds from our garden which helped as well as adding additional veggies. Started off by sauteing some onions, mushrooms, red and green peppers and flash boiled broccoli for 90 sec. Setting these to the side, we focused on the butter/garlic/herb/cream/cheese sauce, adding extra garlic, cayenne pepper, and red pepper flakes. For the pasta we used bow tie since I think they do a better job of picking up the sauce over linguini. All of this was combined in a big pot to heat back up being careful to not over cook the shrimp. Served with some home made garlic bread. It was orgasmic! Will be added to the usual rotation, although I'm confident it was we above the stated 517 calories per serving...

I like to dredge the shrimp in a mix of flour, a little salt /pepper and oregano and then fry them in some olive oil and butter. Remove them from the pan, and then make the sauce. Add the shrimp back to the sauce before serving. Using white wine and fresh mushrooms is always a plus too!
I mixed a teaspoon of corn starch with water and thickened the sauce slightly. The sauce is light and lively and the recipe is awesome!

Since shrimp can be overcooked very easily, and since raw shrimp cooks so quickly (just a few minutes) I chose to use raw. I reduced the cream with a good splash of chicken broth until it somewhat thickened before tossing in the garlic, herbs (I used all fresh and included some chives) and shrimp. Don't think for a minute that the cream makes this a heavy dish with a thick sauce. It is deceptively light, fresh and delicious.

Excellent and fast! Mine looked much different than the photo; more fresh, less creamy. I followed Valerie's recommendation and cooked my shrimp separately with a couple of strong shakes of chili powder, just 3 minutes. I also used fresh basil and parsley. There was a tablespoon of butter on the bottom of the pot, so I might lighten the butter a bit next time.

Agree this is great base. Added garlic powder, onion powder and a bit more whipping cream and cooked on med stirring often until cream thickened. Then added shrimp after cream was thicker. Will even use this as just a cream sauce fir pasta without tye shrimp. Very yummy.
Amazing! Like something from a restaurant!
Made this for a family birthday dinner and it is as a huge hit! I used a fish seasoning on the shrimp instead of salt & pepper. This dish was delicious!!
The sauce was really thin. The presentation looked delicious but it lacked flavor… needs more garlic and more body in the sauce..
It was delicious! So easy to make and a perfect valentine's meal!
Quick, easy and delicious dinner. I made no changes and was pleased I did not. Husband who isn’t a pasta lover said keep this recipe.

Nice and simple. I steamed my shrimp in a steamer basket while boiling my noodles. Did a cold plunge once cooked. We like more sauce, so next time will add more cream. May also add lemon if wine to butter a garlic for added flavor. Used a squirt of lemon after serving and it made all the difference.
Wow! Wonderful!
Lovely over all. I added some wine to the shrimp and would add tomatoes in the future

Perfectly Perfect Pasta! The sauce and shrimp combination are one of the best flavors ever!! Full confession I don’t (or didn’t) particularly care for shrimp. Today I ate 4 of them with this divine pasta dish. My friends aren’t going to believe it. It’s rare I cook a recipe without any changes and today was the rarest. The only mishap was that we ran out of linguine and had to use fettucine. More confessions – my first box of fettucine ripped on the bottom when I opened the top and dry pasta spewed all over the kitchen floor. So, I had just enough pasta in a second box to finish the dish. The pasta gods were on my side today. I took a moment of prayer. My husband and I are so grateful we experienced this very lovely dinner today! Since the pasta was lean today, we had plenty of leftover shrimps and sauced to perfection!!!
